leftEvidence.title: The mourning woman becomes Solomon’s city

points.label: Solomon-relative action
points.left: The interpreting angel identifies the transformed woman as Zion, the city Solomon built, and explains her grief through the Temple’s fall.
points.right: Stephen recalls the wilderness tent, David’s desire, Solomon’s building, and Isaiah’s claim that the Most High does not dwell in handmade houses.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: A visionary figure turns personal mourning into Jerusalem’s remembered history.
points.right: Temple history is honored and relativized within a speech accusing resistant hearers.

payload.posture: 2 Esdras makes Solomon’s city part of Zion’s symbolic grief; Acts places his building under the claim that God is not contained by handmade houses.

rightEvidence.title: Stephen places Solomon’s house under prophetic critique

payload.tension: Later memory can honor the builder’s place in Jerusalem while refusing to equate God with the built place.
payload.title: Solomon’s city remembered and Solomon’s house bounded
